cap: The optic chiasm lies just above the sella, so a macroadenoma growing upward presses first on the crossing fibers from both nasal retinas and removes both temporal fields (bitemporal hemianopia), usually starting in the superior quadrants. A mass growing sideways enters the cavernous sinus, where cranial nerves III, IV, V1, V2 and VI run with the internal carotid artery, causing diplopia and facial numbness.
